summary:
LunaBase OS is an interactive space mission simulator. You will be the Flight Director of your lunar base, having to manage basic resources.

The simulator uses real data from NASA regarding space weather in order to simulate the management of resources on a lunar base. It uses NASA’s DONKI data to show the effects of solar flares and test how you would deal with solar events affecting the safety and functioning of a lunar base. The simulator also uses NASA’s Astronomy Picture of the Day (APOD).

This simulator shows the challenges of setting up a sustainable base on the Moon, using real data from NASA. This should help increase interest in space exploration and give players an insight into planning, decision making and the risks involved with running a lunar base in future.
details:
LunaBase OS is an interactive lunar base simulator that introduces users to the difficulties of setting up a sustainable human presence on the moon.

In this simulation you are a Flight Director. You must manage your lunar base. You need to balance resources such as oxygen, food and electricity. Every decision you make will affect how well your lunar base is doing. It helps you to think strategically about your limited resources.

This project includes real NASA data. The software accesses data relating to solar flares from NASA’s DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information). This adds real life aspects to the lunar base simulation. We have shown how difficult it would be to protect our lunar base and astronauts from solar activity. We have also used NASA’s APOD (Astronomy Picture Of The Day) API. This shows us astronomical images along with a description.

We have created the application using Python. We used the Streamlit library to create the application. We have used the Requests library to access data from NASA’s online APIs. This means you don’t need any specialist equipment to run the application as it can be run in a web browser.

Our application includes strategic game elements, space science and real data. This means we aren’t just giving the user theoretical information. They will get to make some decisions about running the lunar base. This will help make space science more interactive and engaging. It will also help increase awareness of the technological challenges they may face when going to the Moon in the future.
